SUMMARY

S&P Global Inc.(SPGI-0.44%)reported third quarter results highlighted by a strategic review of its Capital IQ and associated Kensho data businesses to prioritize investments in its leading credit, equities, and commodities markets. Management reported accelerated revenue growth in indices, energy, and market intelligence divisions, supported by a 4,000% year-over-year increase in API call volume and the normalization of AI intellectual property rights in customer contracts. The company raised its full-year guidance for organic revenue growth, operating margin expansion, and adjusted earnings per share following record build issuance through the first nine months of the year. The company confirmed it remains on track to return more than $7 billion to shareholders through repurchases by year end while maintaining a flat year-over-year headcount through productivity gains and AI integration.

Operator:Good morning, and welcome to S&P Global's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. I would like to inform you that this call is being recorded for broadcast. All participants are in a listen-only mode. We will open the conference to questions and answers after the presentation and instructions will follow at that time. Mark Grant:Good morning, and thank you for joining today's&P Global Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Presenting on today's call are Martina L. Cheung, President and Chief Executive Officer and Eric Walter Aboaf, Chief Financial Officer. In addition, Kathy Clay, CEO of S and P Dow Jones Indices, will be joining for the Q&A portion of today's call. We issued a press release with our results earlier today. In addition, we have posted a supplemental slide deck with additional information on our results and guidance. If you need a copy of the release and financial schedules, or the supplemental deck, they can be downloaded at investor.spglobal.com.

The matters discussed in today's conference call may contain forward looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 2 thousand including projections, estimates, and descriptions of future events. Any such statements are based on current expectations and current economic conditions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from results anticipated in these forward looking statements. The financial metrics we will be discussing today refer to non GAAP adjusted metrics unless explicitly noted otherwise.

All financial information presented in the earnings documents and to be discussed on today's call reflect the company's results on a continuing operations basis unless otherwise stated, and prior periods have been recast accordingly to conform to this current presentation. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to Martina L. Cheung. Martina?

Martina L. Cheung:Thank you, Mark, and thank you to everyone joining us this morning. I am also very pleased to have Kathy Clay, CEO of S and P Dow Jones Indices, with us for the Q&A portion of the call. I will start with the bigger picture before I get into the quarter. Our strategy rests on 3 priorities. Advancing our market leadership, expanding into high growth adjacencies, and amplifying our enterprise capabilities and AI. Today, we are taking the next step on that first priority, sharpening our focus on the markets where we lead, S and P Global is the trust anchor in 3 of the world's most important markets. Credit, equities, and commodities.

The strategic review we announced this morning is about putting our investment where we are strongest. Now turning to the quarter. We delivered solid performance in the quarter, driven by strong execution and deep engagement with our customers, and our AI initiatives are starting to show real traction. Revenue growth accelerated in indices, energy, and market intelligence, and we expanded margins in each of these divisions. Ratings revenue growth decelerated modestly as we expected, but the point I would make is that the durable profitable growth of our benchmark franchise remains robust. Benchmark's revenue increased 7%, and total recurring revenue across the enterprise increased 8%.

With acceleration in subscription revenue, strong incremental margins, and continued productivity gains, we delivered 60 basis points of margin expansion in the quarter. On capital return, we have repurchased $4 billion in shares so far this year, and we are on track to complete more than $7 billion in repurchases by year end. We are also seeing real improvement in customer traction, in our speed of execution. And that helped to drive revenue growth acceleration in both market intelligence and energy. Our benchmarks remain critical components of market infrastructure across credit, equities, and commodities. Supply chain diversification and data centers are topics in nearly every customer conversation we have.

And our customers are turning to S and P Global more than ever to make their most important decisions. As you saw in the release this morning, we also announced a strategic review for Capital IQ and its associated data businesses, which I will be discussing more in a moment. Turning to the operating environment. This year has brought geopolitical conflict, shifting rates, and swings in commodity markets. But also strong activity across credit and equity markets. Our clients have remained resilient, And as AI and massive capital investment reshape markets, what we are seeing is that trusted benchmarks and data matter more than ever. In the debt markets, there was strong demand for rated debt in the quarter.

The issuance environment was favorable, with the impact of higher treasury yields offset by continued near record tight credit spreads. And S and P Global remains the rating agency of choice for AI related and hyperscaler issuance. We continue to see above average returns in the US equities market, and we made good progress in high growth adjacencies like DeFi and prediction markets. In energy, customers are adapting to geopolitical and supply chain volatility. Our global trading services business stabilized in the third quarter. And renewals are returning to the levels we saw prior to the Iran conflict. Demand for our AI products is also very strong.

During the quarter, we combined our MCP tools and adaptive retrieval agents, into 1 holistic AI data portal offering. Demand for our mission critical data is very strong, and we launched ratings, energy, and visible alpha data in MCP. During the quarter. What we hear consistently from customers is that they are choosing S&P Global Data because it is highly performant with lower error rates compared to other providers. And our adaptive retrieval agents are also resonating strongly with customers. We signed a large multiyear competitive displacement in the quarter, that combined Cap IQ with our AI data portal solutions from Market Intelligence.

We also signed a very large deal with a global energy company that combined an upstream win back with our AI-ready data. Negotiations with customers on AI rights are normalizing, and we are signing deals with robust pricing, that protect our IP. Customers see the value in leveraging our AI-ready data while respecting our intellectual property. Sales cycles stabilized, following some temporary noise last quarter, contributing to the acceleration in subscription revenue growth in both market intelligence and energy. The strength of the S and P Global Ratings franchise was clear in the third quarter. With total build issuance up 8% year over year.

The first 3 quarters of this year are the 3 strongest quarters on record for build issuance. Hyperscaler issuance remained strong in the quarter, bringing the year to date total to approximately $240 billion, and we continue to expect between $250 billion and $300 billion for the full year. We have seen continued strength in investment grade issuance outside of the hyperscalers. Excluding hyperscaler issuance in the third quarter, investment grade issuance would have increased around 15%. While total build issuance would have been up low single digits. We expect issuance to remain robust in absolute terms, but we are lapping a difficult year over year compare in the second half.

Our updated guidance assumes high single digit build issuance growth for the full year reflecting our continued expectations for $250 billion to $300 billion hyperscaler issuance. We now expect 20% to 30% growth in M&A issuance this year given the strength of M&A related issuance in the third quarter. Moving on to indices. S&P Dow Jones Indices remains the global leader in indices, both in terms of assets under management and in index based derivatives. We had more than $600 billion in net inflows into our ETF products, and we ended the quarter with ETF assets under management up 26%. Continued market volatility drove a 15% in average daily volumes for our exchange traded derivatives.

The strength of this franchise creates powerful opportunities for partnerships and collaboration in new and existing markets. We announced several agreements in the last few months that demonstrate the importance of partnering with S&P Dow Jones Indices, for leading market participants. The extension of our 500 options agreement with CBOE solidifies our partnership through the next 25 years and creates meaningful value for customers and shareholders. We are actively pursuing opportunities to expand the addressable market for our intellectual property in areas like prediction markets. And we continue to innovate and explore opportunities in partnerships that take advantage of the rapid innovation in this space. Enabling our customers to leverage our products in new ways.

We do not expect these announcements to have a meaningful impact on 2026 financial results. But we do expect to benefit in 2027 and beyond. As we expected, energy revenue growth accelerated in the quarter, though energy and commodities markets remain volatile. Oil prices remain elevated, and we expect oil to stay around $100 per barrel through the fourth quarter. We saw better traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with flows reaching almost 2-thirds pre-war levels. That made it easier for customers to transact with confidence and drive subscription growth in the quarter. We are also seeing market participants return to the derivative products based on our benchmark prices, as traders and others adjust to more volatile markets.

LNG refined products and chemicals remain more constrained. And our customers are using our data to help identify and plan for alternative sources and partnerships. I would also say our recent acquisition of Data Center Hawk could not have been timelier. Combined with 1 Research, S and P Global is now a leading provider of data and insights. Demand for data center build out is unprecedented. With our teams forecasting significant increases in demand for power, chips, and materials to deliver that infrastructure. In fact, our team forecasts nearly $900 billion of CapEx this year for the 6 largest hyperscalers, nearly doubling from 2025 levels.

The intensity of investment in this area is benefiting every 1 of our divisions, highlighting the growing convergence between financial markets and commodity markets. Obviously, this year, debt issuance and equity valuations have been driven higher by AI and data center investments. Demand is also increasing for supply chain insights, counterparty credit analytics, power forecasts, and logistics data, among financial services and industrial customers who need to understand these dynamics in-depth. Demand for our AI products is strong. For several quarters, customers using our AI solutions have increased their spend with us at a much faster rate than average. In market intelligence, ACV growth is now 1.8x the growth rate of non AI customers. In energy, it remains approximately 3x.

This is a strong signal of the value of our AI solutions to our customers. Over time, we believe growth rates will converge as more of our customers become AI customers. API call volume grew rapidly, up nearly 50% since Q2 and more than 4 thousand% year over year. More customers are expanding in house solutions and integrations with Frontier models powered by our data. Negotiations with customers on AI rights are normalizing, and we are signing deals with robust pricing that protect our IP. As I mentioned earlier, that comes down to the quality of our AI tools, and our unique datasets like Visible Alpha. Turning to slide 11.

We announced today that we have initiated a strategic review of alternatives for Capital IQ and its associated data businesses within Market Intelligence, including their potential separation. The businesses being considered for separation include the Capital IQ and the Kensho data and platforms businesses within Market Intelligence. While the exact perimeter remains under review, we expect to retain ratings direct, and ratings express as well as Enterprise Solutions. These businesses operate at scale with high recurring revenue and a large, long-standing base of more than 15 thousand clients and more than 355 thousand users. Demand for their trusted data continues to grow, as customers increasingly seek to integrate it directly into their own systems and tools.

We are confident in the ability of these businesses to create incredible value for our customers while rapidly innovating to bring differentiated data and insights to the market in an AI first way. We believe separate ownership would give them the dedicated investment and focus needed to continue the revenue growth acceleration and rapid innovation that we delivered this quarter. Given the commercial and data relationships between S&P Global and the business under review, we would seek to keep our interest closely aligned in any transaction.

At the same time, a more focused S and P Global would allow us to prioritize investment and reinforce our strengths in the markets where we have the strongest position, and are best enabled to create value. S and P Global is deeply embedded in the world's credit equities and commodities markets. Providing trusted benchmarks, mission critical data, and insights that are essential to how those markets operate. Our expected go forward portfolio benefits from durable secular tailwinds and attractive incremental margins. This allows us to invest while delivering consistent margin expansion over time.

We expect that when and if this process is completed, S and P Global will be a focused and synergistic organization of high growth businesses positioned for strong growth in organic revenue, profits, and EPS. We believe this portfolio can also generate significant free cash flow enhancing our capital allocation flexibility, and ultimately, our ability to return capital to shareholders. There is no definitive timetable for completing this strategic review. What I can tell you is that maintaining continuity for our customers and our colleagues throughout this process is of the utmost importance.

Existing contracts and service commitments remain in place, and we will ensure that our valued customers continue to receive the innovative products, differentiated data that they rely on today. While this process is underway, we will be thoughtful about the impact it could have on our customers, our people and our shareholders. We will provide updates at appropriate times, but we are very early in this process. And we expect the earliest meaningful update we would be able to provide will be on our February earnings call. With subscription growth accelerating, margins expanding, and an improving outlook, we are pleased with the excellent results we delivered in the third quarter.

We are excited about the opportunities to come for Capital IQ and its related businesses, and we are excited about the prospects for S and P Global. We look forward to finishing the year strong. Now I will hand it over to Eric to take you through the details of the quarter and the guidance.

Eric Walter Aboaf:Thank you, Martina, and good morning, everyone. Starting with Slide 14, We delivered a strong third quarter financial result with 7% revenue growth both on an organic constant currency and all in basis as M&A and FX had only modest net impacts. We saw revenue acceleration in 3 of our 4 divisions, which I will come back to shortly. Adjusted expenses grew 5% as we invested in key growth areas, funded with productivity initiatives and held total headcount flat year over year. We thus delivered 60 basis points of year on year margin expansion to 53.5%. Excluding Astra from the prior year period, our third quarter 2026 margin expansion would have been up 120 basis points.

We delivered 8% growth in adjusted operating profit and 9% growth in EPS, driven by more than $6 billion in share repurchases over the last 12 months, including another $2.6 billion in share buybacks launched in the third quarter, EPS growth was partly tempered by the timing of tax expenses. in the quarter. I will now turn to our divisions, starting with ratings on Slide 15. Ratings revenue grew 2% in the quarter. As expected, growth moderated from the first half of the year against tougher comparisons. Issuance was up 8% and transaction revenue increased 1%.

Both were led by considerable strength in investment grade up 28%, benefited from several large M&A and hyperscaler deals, partly offset by high yield bank loans and structured finance, all of which had difficult prior year comparisons. This quarter, the mix shift out of high yield and bank loans into investment grade led to a wider than usual variance between billed issuance growth and transaction revenue growth. However, year to date, that variance shrinks to less than 2 percentage points, with issuance and revenue growth up 15%, 13%, respectively. We expect build issuance growth to generally mirror transaction revenue growth over time. Nontransaction revenue grew 4% primarily driven by higher annual fee revenue as well as CRISIL.

Growth in nontransaction decelerated modestly given the much tougher comparison which will continue into the fourth quarter as well. When looking at combined transaction and non transaction revenue, as you can see on the slide, the 10% growth in financials and 8% growth in CRISIL and other revenue was tempered somewhat by the slower growth in governments and corporates, as well as a modest decline in structured finance. All that said, we are also very pleased to have closed the OwenZeppelin acquisition yesterday, gives us a leading position in the smart contract space and reinforces our progress in DeFi.

Adjusted expenses increased by 7% driven by higher compensation costs and continued investments in strategic initiatives partially offset by our productivity efforts. While margins contracted approximately 130 basis points in the quarter, this can be impacted by the timing of expenses. Year to date, ratings margins have expanded just over 100 basis points. Now turning to S and P Dow Jones Indices on Slide 16. Indices maintained its strong momentum, reporting the 14th consecutive quarter of record revenue. Revenue in the quarter grew 20% with strength in both asset linked fees and exchange traded derivatives.

Revenues associated with asset linked fees grew 24% year over year with growth driven by a balanced mix of market appreciation, and net inflows into products based on S and P Dow Jones indices. As the world's largest index business by AUM, we achieved a new record quarter for ETF AUM of $6.5 trillion in the quarter, and our strategic initiatives are contributing to a number 1 ranking in total ETF market flow capture among index providers. Exchange traded derivatives revenue increased 19% its fourth consecutive quarter of double digit growth, led by strength in SPX ETD volumes. Last month, as Martina mentioned, together with CBOE Global Markets, we announced the extension of our exclusive licensing agreement through 2051.

The new agreement builds on more than 40 years of collaboration and positions us well to drive further innovation and growth. The contract extension will not impact 2026 financial results, but we do expect a couple percentage points of incremental total index revenue growth in 2027. We will provide more detail when we give 2027 guidance in February. Data and custom subscriptions revenue grew 7% or 5% organically. Supported by continued new business growth in end of day contracts. Adjusted expenses were up 14% year over year driven by investments in growth initiatives, and higher compensation costs. Indices operating profit grew 22% and operating margin expanded a 150 basis points to 71.9%.

Now turning to S and P Global Energy on Slide 17. Energy revenue rebounded to 6% on both a reported and organic constant currency basis, benefiting from continued strong demand for Platts benchmarks. As well as our differentiated data research and thought leadership. We delivered this healthy growth despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and the negative impact of sanctions worth about half a point. In the third quarter, we saw improvements in the operating environment. Impacted customers in the Middle East have begun to stabilize and adapt to the current landscape. This was reflected in our accelerating organic growth rising sales, and solid GTS volumes.

The near term environment remains uncertain, but we continue to believe these headwinds are transitory and we continue to expect organic constant currency growth to normalize in 2027 to within the 6% to 8% average range we outlined at our 2025 Investor Day. Sera grew 5% or 6% organically when accounting for the divestiture of Upstream Software. Organic growth benefited from the broad based increases across our offerings particularly insights and analytics and consulting. We remain pleased to see ongoing traction in our upstream data transformation with a return to positive revenue growth and encouraging feedback from our early customers of Titan. Platts revenue increased 7% in the quarter, driven by strong growth in price assessments.

Growth in GTS revenues stabilized from last quarter as well despite a challenging compare from last year. The third quarter of 2025 and the third quarter of 2026 were tied for the second highest quarterly revenue on record As Martina mentioned, demand for our AI products has been very strong, and our discrete AI products and energy contributed around 50 basis points to our revenue growth this quarter. Adjusted expenses grew by just 2% driving margin expansion of 190 basis points to 48.1%. Energy's modest expense growth in the quarter was driven by higher technology and compensation costs, almost fully offset by productivity programs and expense discipline. Turning to Market Intelligence on Slide 18.

Revenue growth accelerated to 7% on both the reported and organic constant currency basis in the third quarter, We saw particular strength in Kensho Data and Platforms, and Kensho Data itself was Market Intelligence's fastest growing business. We remain encouraged by the strong customer adoption and demand for our AI-ready data. Similar to our energy division, our discrete AI products contributed approximately 0.5 a point of growth to Kensho Data and Platforms this quarter. Sales cycles have normalized following a slight elongation last quarter. And we are no longer seeing a negative impact to revenue growth. In fact, we saw a small benefit in the quarter from some true ups on contracts that renewed after the second quarter ended.

We saw improved sales and renewal rates in 3Q, as we closed on several of the large deals that have extended from second quarter while also ensuring that our intellectual property was protected for the long term. In the third quarter, subscription revenue grew 6%, and 7% on an organic basis, benefiting from broad based growth across our subscription franchises. Kensho Data and Platforms revenue growth accelerated to 10% or 6% organically. Saw acceleration in Kensho data driven by strong adoption of our AI-ready data feeds with growth comfortably in the double digits. Enterprise solutions reported revenue grew 2% reflecting the divestiture of EDM and ThinkFolio while organic revenue was up a strong 8%.

This was driven by broad based growth across products particularly in lending solutions like WSO. Enterprise Solutions organic subscription revenue grew 7% also driven by strength across products. This performance really demonstrated the critical nature of these products in our customers' workflows and also in the markets themselves. Market Intelligence's adjusted expenses increased 5% year over year, driven by inorganic expenses from the Wit Intelligence acquisition as well as higher technology costs, partially offset by the impact of recent divestitures and productivity programs. Market Intelligence delivered 110 basis points of operating margin expansion to 36.2% in the quarter. Now shifting to our outlook starting with Slide 19.

As a reminder, with our spin of Mobility completed on July 1, mobility results were moved to discontinued operations. Consistent with the guidance we provided in the second quarter, our full year guide on both the GAAP and adjusted basis excludes the contributions from Mobility for the whole year. Slide 19 outlines our GAAP guidance. Slide 20 shows our adjusted guidance. Given the outperformance in both ratings and indices year to date, we are raising our full year guidance for organic constant currency growth to a range of 7.5% to 8.5%. We are also increasing our guidance for adjusted operating margin expansion. We now expect total operating margin expansion in the range of 75 to 100 basis points.

Excluding the impact of Astra, which was divested late last year, we would expect margin expansion of 125 to 150 basis points. While we expect slightly higher interest expense as a result of the expected bond offering later this quarter, we expect the EPS impact to be more than offset by lower corporate unallocated expense and a lower share count. So we are raising our guidance for adjusted EPS as well to a range of $17.70 to $17.95. Now turning to our division guidance on Slide 21. As I mentioned, we are raising our outlook for ratings. Given our expectation for high single digit build issuance for the year.

We now expect organic constant currency revenue growth of 6.5% to 8%. In the fourth quarter, this implies a slight decline year over year in transaction revenue, as we have been signaling all year and a modest growth in non transaction revenue as we lap a difficult comparison from the fourth quarter of last year. For the full year, we expect ratings margin expansion to be towards the lower end of the 75 to 100 basis point range we just discussed for the company as a whole. For indices, we now expect organic constant currency growth in the range of 17% to 18.5%, as we continue to benefit from strong equity valuations and strong net flows.

For the full year, we expect indices margins to be towards the higher end of the 75 to 100 basis point company range. For energy, there is some nuance to the upstream software divestiture that impacts reported revenue growth in both the third quarter and the fourth quarter. Just due to the timing. We continue to expect organic constant currency growth of 4.5% to 6 for the full year. However, the upstream software divestiture was completed on September 1, so only 1 month of that impact was seen in the reported results in 3Q. We will see a full quarter's impact in the fourth quarter, so the delta between organic and reported revenue growth will be wider in Q4.

We also saw a benefit from very strong onetime sales in the third quarter that are harder to predict and may not reoccur in the fourth quarter. Importantly, on an organic constant currency basis, we expect subscription growth to continue to improve in the fourth quarter. For the full year, we expect margin expansion in Energy to be strong, but modestly below the range we are guiding to for the full company. Margin in the fourth quarter will be negatively impacted by inorganic activity including the absence of upstream software and the addition of Data Center Hawk.

For market intelligence for the full year, we continue to expect organic constant currency growth of 5.5% to 7%, though with only 2 months left in the year, we are reasonably comfortable that we will be slightly above the midpoint of that range. For the full year, we expect margin expansion near the high end of the range we discussed for the whole company. Lastly, for the fourth quarter, we expect adjusted free cash flow of approximately $1.6 billion With that, let me turn the call back over to Mark for your questions.

Mark Grant:Thank you, Eric. Those on the line, if you would like to ask a question, please press 1 and record your name. Cancel or withdraw your question, simply press pound 2. For those joining via telephone, please turn off speakerphone in order to optimize sound quality. Participants will be limited to 1 question in order to allow time for others during today's Operator, we will now take the first question.

Operator:Thank you. Our first question comes from Ashish Sabadra with RBC Capital Markets. Your line is open.

Ashish Sabadra:Thanks for taking my question. Congrats on the solid quarter and announcing the strategic review. My question was just around the timing. Why did you decide to launch the strategic review now? And also, as we think about the remainco, how does the strategic review enhance both the financial profile as well as the quality of the Remainco? Thanks.

Martina L. Cheung:Hi, Ashish, it is Martina. Thanks so much for the Maybe just to comment on the timing and why now. This is really a function of long-term positioning. For both S and P Global as well as Cap IQ and the associated businesses. And think it is important to recognize that as we enter into this review, we are coming at it from a position of strength, really. With Cap IQ and the associated data businesses. You saw that acceleration in the third quarter, particularly on Kensho Data. Where the commercial execution and just the growing demand for our super high quality and performance data is really taking hold. And so we are excited about that.

You also have seen that we are the trust anchor for 3 of the world's most important markets. The credit markets, the equity markets, the commodities markets. And so, you know, while we have the potential to see if under a new owner, the KDP portions of the business that are in the perimeter could grow faster, could innovate faster, we also have an opportunity to look at a more focused portfolio within S and P Global and then make sure that we are actually focusing our investments in the markets where we are leading and where we are the strongest. And also, that would result in, I think, a very favorable financial profile.

Eric, do you want to comment on that?

Eric Walter Aboaf:Yeah, Ashish, I would just say it is premature at this point. We are working down. Working through the perimeter of potential review and potential separation as we learn more, we will certainly come back to you and certainly by the February earnings call, we will look forward to giving you more of an update Thanks, Ashish.

Martina L. Cheung:Thank you.

Operator:Our next question comes from Toni Kaplan. With Morgan Stanley. Your line is open.

Toni Kaplan:Thanks so much. I also wanted to ask a little bit about the review. You have said in the past that Cap IQ is approximately 6% of revenue. Sounds like maybe there are some additional pieces of Kensho data and platforms that are being considered here. And so I was wondering if there was any way to give either a range or a approximate size and. Inclusive of this additional data. And I know there was a Bloomberg article about this early last month, and so just wondering if you have had any inbounds in the meantime. Thank you.

Martina L. Cheung:Hi, Toni. Thanks for the question. I would say that the businesses under review here are the Cap IQ business and the associated data businesses. So those data businesses would include, financials, F&L, Visible alpha. And what we said is what is not in the perimeter is enterprise solutions ratings direct. And ratings express. Now it is a review, and so, you know, the overall fine tuning, if you like, of the perimeter, obviously, is going to occur as we continue through this evaluation and the process and something we can come back on. We certainly expect to come back with more clarity potentially on that in February when we do our earnings call.

Maybe on the process itself and if we have had inbounds. Eric, do you want to comment on that?

Eric Walter Aboaf:Sure. Toni, we have had a good amount of, work that we have been, doing over the last month in particular in terms of, you know, the perimeter as Martina described. We have also been front footed in terms of going out and exploring interest. We have gotten quite a bit of interest from a number of different potential-- potential firms on the other side. You know, we have gone ahead and signed NDAs with a number of them. You know, we have engaged with advisers. So we are, you know, we are tackling this expeditiously. Obviously, there is no certainty of an outcome 1 way or the other.

But we are we are tackling this expeditiously and certainly update you as we as we have more to share.

Martina L. Cheung:Thanks, Toni.

Operator:Our next question comes from Faiza Alwy with Deutsche Bank. Your line is open.

Faiza Alwy:Yes, hi. Thank you. Good morning. I wanted to ask about the ratings business. Martina, I believe your ratings research team just put out something in the last day or so, a forecast slower market issuance in 2027. Which I know is different from build issuance. And I know it is early but it would be great to hear your take on, if the strong issuance growth this year indicates perhaps slower growth next year and how we should think about the puts and takes under various macro and credit scenarios.

Martina L. Cheung:Hi, Faiza. Thanks so much for the question. Yes, it is a little bit too early for 2027 commentary. Look, we look forward to providing more specifics on that in February. Now that said, I would say we look at this market overall over the medium term as being high growth with, very strong secular tailwinds. And it is an area where we have extremely strong refinancing walls around 11 trillion over the next 4 years. We also see continued demand in areas like private credit, huge demand in project finance, and we also see incredible appetite, I think, for structured finance as well as investment grade.

In fact, we pay, as you know, a lot of attention to fund flows, and we have seen quite a good deal of inflows into investment grade funds this year, which we have seen has been a very solid appetite for some of the larger deals that have been done by the hyperscalers. So, and I think maybe just 1 comment on the hyperscaler growth and. You know, because that was such a factor this year, and certainly, it was faster than we thought it was gonna be. So you saw us raise our estimate for the full year for hyperscaler growth. that is an area where we will look at the announced CapEx from the hyperscalers into 2027.

And similar to what we did this year, we will make an assessment of how much of that we think will be funded by the debt markets versus the equity markets. And we will also make an assessment on how much we think will be actually done in year. And some of the leading indicators we are paying attention to there will include the remaining performance obligations of the hyperscalers, which is a good indication of go forward growth and demand. Those RPOs or remaining performance obligations remain quite high.

The latest visible alpha cell site estimates there for 4 of those hyperscalers is just under $3 trillion for 2027. it is not a, you know, it is not a forecast of CapEx. it is a good leading indicator and reference point, though, for how we think this is going to play out Thanks for the question.

Eric Walter Aboaf:Jeffrey, I think as we have described before, as we have expanded our planned buyback for the year, which is expected now to be $7 billion twice the original $3.5 billion that we announced back in February. We will be issuing a little more debt. The expectation right now is about $2 billion of debt at prevailing market rates, and that obviously factors into interest expense that we will we will actually cover. Thanks.

And what we are focused on, as you can see from the margin expansion we have delivered, that each year, we plan and budget for a couple of points of productivity gains across the board. Some of that is directly AI. Some of that is non AI. Most of it is actually mixed and integrated, Because that is how we transform the company. And what we are doing with that, is, some of that productivity literally gets reinvested in our growth feature functionality and product launches because that is how we want to direct it, and then some, we deliver to the bottom line. Thanks, Craig.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Andrew Steinerman with JPMorgan. Your line is open.

Andrew Steinerman:Hi. Could you just review some of the puts and takes S&P assumed as fourth quarter credit issuance, specifically talking about AI And when I say AI associated, do not just mean hyperscaler financing for the fourth quarter. I know fourth quarter could be a brief quarter for issuance seasonally. I also have a very small brief housekeeping question. Could you provide us the organic constant currency revenue growth I am sorry, ACV growth for MI. The ACV growth for MI on a OCC basis.

Eric Walter Aboaf:Andrew, it is Eric. There are, a number of the puts and takes for fourth quarter issuances. We certainly expect investment grade to continue to be a good tailwind We talked about the double digit growth there, and that will continue. There will probably be some continued offset with rising rates around high yield and leverage loans and so forth, and then governments we will kind of see as they play out. So those kinds of puts and takes, I think hyperscaler issuance, we described how, we have had quite a bit of issuances so far through the third quarter, but we expect several more in the fourth quarter, and that will be a nice tailwind.

So a number of different moving parts. Back on 7% organic constant currency. And then ACV came in nicely around 6.5 percent. You know, ticked up a bit from the 6% range. it is something we are pleased with and, you know, it demonstrates the momentum we are seeing in the business, and, and the underlying, traction that we are seeing with our with our clients.

Martina L. Cheung:Thanks, Andrew.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Owen Lau with Clear Street. Your line is open.

Owen Lau:Hi, good morning. Thank you for taking my question. I have a broader picture question. Given the spin off of Mobility and now the strategic review for CapIQ, and, Martina, could you please talk about what will S and P Global look like in 3 years and which area do you think S and P can drive faster revenue growth after all these restructuring? Then I have a quick 1 for Kathy. Good to hear from you, by the way. So it looks like Kalshi, it is a preferred relationship, but not exclusive. Could you please comment on what that means and why not making these exclusive just like your relationship with Cboe? Thank you.

Catherine R. Clay:Hi, Owen. it is Kathy. Thanks for the question. I am gonna start with you. In the prediction markets, as I mentioned, this is very, very new terrain. And so, you know, we are wanting to partner with those that have the most opportunity in the space. Kalshi, of course, is the largest prediction market as of today. But also, Owen, as I mentioned, we are excited to continue to innovate with our other partners like Cboe and CME in this space. And so, you know, that is an appropriate strategy when there is a lot of unknowns in a new market.

And so we are just looking forward to working with these different partners and really finding the opportunity set. So that is that is exactly what we are-- what we are doing, Owen. And I will pass it to Martina.

Martina L. Cheung:Thanks, Kathy. Owen, I think for, for S&P Global, the way for all of us and for our shareholders to think about this particular review that we have announced is that we did not announce a change in the strategy. For S and P Global. Our priorities are consistent with what we set out at IR day last year, which is around advancing our market leadership, expanding into high growth adjacencies, and expanding our enterprise capabilities and AI. And, really, the Cap IQ and associated data business review that we announced is getting at advancing our market leadership. it is that first priority.

What that allows us to do, if we do actually execute a transaction here, is to have an S and P Global that is focused in the areas where we are clear leaders in the debt markets, the equity markets, and the commodity markets, with unique benchmarks, differentiated IP coming from those benchmarks, and critical tools, mission-critical workflows and models that inform trillions of dollars of decision every year. that is really how I would encourage you to think about it over the next several years. This does not necessarily change anything that we would have to do with, in fact, it does not change anything within indices, within ratings, or within energy.

This is really about the market intelligence businesses and specifically Cap IQ and the associated businesses. But I would look at the go forward S and P Global portfolio as a very strong portfolio with very unique assets and more flexibility around capital allocation, including returning capital to shareholders. Thanks, Owen.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Jason Haas with Wells Fargo. Your line is open.

Jason Haas:You talk about how integrated Cap IQ and the other businesses under review are with the rest of S and P? And maybe you could compare to how integrated they are versus, what we saw with mobility.

Martina L. Cheung:Hi, Jason. I would say that there are cross-divisional commercial agreements. So for example, the ratings analyst actually use Cap IQ and then we have. Obviously, we have got a little bit of sort of a data foundation under CapIQ helps with some other parts of the business as well. I would not say that this is deeply complicated in the sense that for example, enterprise solutions has completely different technology underpinning their platforms. And everything else outside of KDP is separate. Ratings is on their own stack. Index is on their own stack. And energy is on their own stack.

And so you know, we have actually been paying very close attention to how integrated this is, and I think we have proven frankly, that we can do large complicated transactions We have a team that has, you know, solid playbook on large M&A, and this is 1 where we have got working and we are pretty happy that we have got the capabilities in hand to do this without disruption to our customers and to our shareholders. Thanks for the question.

Operator:Thank you. We will now take our final question from Jeffrey Meuler with Baird. Your line is open.

Jeffrey Meuler:Yes. Thank you. Can you just talk more on how you are structuring the AI Ready data distribution deals in terms of contract duration and revenue terms to continue to grow alongside your clients as they ramp usage in addition to continuing to grow as you make more datasets available and add logos? Thanks.

Martina L. Cheung:Hi, Jeffrey. Thanks for the question. I would say that, the deals themselves that we have seen really nice price increases on broader renewals. And that has helped to drive subscription growth. We would expect to continue to see that. As well. Now, what I would say is as our clients are looking at the adaptive retrieval products in particular, and this is the agents where you can essentially query more-- do more nuanced queries across multiple datasets from S and P Global. that is where we are seeing a potential for consumption based pricing models and it also complements just the increased interest in new datasets that we are seeing with our clients.

And I would go back to the first client that we announced last quarter as a good example for the adaptive retrieval, that client was taking adaptive retrieval for the existing datasets for which they were licensed but also with a view to licensing new datasets also because they knew they could get, you know, some very good performance from the agent across more datasets. And so that is how we are working. Sally and the team in particular, in the Kensho Data and Platforms business are partnering very closely. there is just huge client engagement around this.

And I think that we will, over time, see growth rates converge here, you know, between the AI growth rates and normal growth rates as more and more of our clients actually adopt and move to AI type products. Thanks for the question, Jeffrey.

Operator:Alright.

Martina L. Cheung:Well, before we close, let me say huge thank you to all of our people at S and P Global for driving the great results we delivered this quarter. I also wanted to give a special thank you to Steven Kempz, who is retiring as our chief legal officer more than a decade, Steven has been a trusted colleague and an excellent source of wisdom and insight for me. Our leadership team, and our board of directors. And I am excited for our new Chief Legal Officer, Thomas Kim, who has already hit the ground running. We want to extend a warm welcome to Thomas and wish Steven all the best in his well earned retirement.

And thank you all again for joining the call this morning.

Operator:Good morning, and welcome to S&P Global's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. I would like to inform you that this call is being recorded for broadcast. All participants are in a listen-only mode. We will open the conference to questions and answers after the presentation and instructions will follow at that time. To access the webcast and slides, go to investor.spglobal.com. If you need any additional technical assistance, please press 0, and I will-- I would now like to introduce Mr. Mark Grant, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer for S and P Global. Sir, you may begin.

Mark Grant:Good morning, and thank you for joining today's&P Global Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Presenting on today's call are Martina L. Cheung, President and Chief Executive Officer and Eric Walter Aboaf, Chief Financial Officer. In addition, Kathy Clay, CEO of S and P Dow Jones Indices, will be joining for the Q&A portion of today's call. We issued a press release with our results earlier today. In addition, we have posted a supplemental slide deck with additional information on our results and guidance. If you need a copy of the release and financial schedules, or the supplemental deck, they can be downloaded at investor.spglobal.com.

The matters discussed in today's conference call may contain forward looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 2 thousand including projections, estimates, and descriptions of future events. Any such statements are based on current expectations and current economic conditions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from results anticipated in these forward looking statements. Additional information concerning these risks and uncertainties can be found in our Forms 10-K and 10-Q filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. In today's earnings documents and during the conference call, we are providing non GAAP financial information.

This information is provided to enable investors to make meaningful comparisons of the company's operating performance between periods and to view the company's business from the same perspective as management. The earnings release contains financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP that corresponds to the non GAAP measures we are providing, and the press release and the supplemental deck contain reconciliations of such GAAP and non GAAP measures. The financial metrics we will be discussing today refer to non GAAP adjusted metrics unless explicitly noted otherwise.

All financial information presented in the earnings documents and to be discussed on today's call reflect the company's results on a continuing operations basis unless otherwise stated, and prior periods have been recast accordingly to conform to this current presentation. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to Martina L. Cheung. Martina?

Martina L. Cheung:Thank you, Mark, and thank you to everyone joining us this morning. I am also very pleased to have Kathy Clay, CEO of S and P Dow Jones Indices, with us for the Q&A portion of the call. I will start with the bigger picture before I get into the quarter. Our strategy rests on 3 priorities. Advancing our market leadership, expanding into high growth adjacencies, and amplifying our enterprise capabilities and AI. Today, we are taking the next step on that first priority, sharpening our focus on the markets where we lead, S and P Global is the trust anchor in 3 of the world's most important markets. Credit, equities, and commodities.

The strategic review we announced this morning is about putting our investment where we are strongest. Now turning to the quarter. We delivered solid performance in the quarter, driven by strong execution and deep engagement with our customers, and our AI initiatives are starting to show real traction. Revenue growth accelerated in indices, energy, and market intelligence, and we expanded margins in each of these divisions. Ratings revenue growth decelerated modestly as we expected, but the point I would make is that the durable profitable growth of our benchmark franchise remains robust. Benchmark's revenue increased 7%, and total recurring revenue across the enterprise increased 8%.

With acceleration in subscription revenue, strong incremental margins, and continued productivity gains, we delivered 60 basis points of margin expansion in the quarter. On capital return, we have repurchased $4 billion in shares so far this year, and we are on track to complete more than $7 billion in repurchases by year end. We are also seeing real improvement in customer traction, in our speed of execution. And that helped to drive revenue growth acceleration in both market intelligence and energy. Our benchmarks remain critical components of market infrastructure across credit, equities, and commodities. Supply chain diversification and data centers are topics in nearly every customer conversation we have.

And our customers are turning to S and P Global more than ever to make their most important decisions. As you saw in the release this morning, we also announced a strategic review for Capital IQ and its associated data businesses, which I will be discussing more in a moment. Turning to the operating environment. This year has brought geopolitical conflict, shifting rates, and swings in commodity markets. But also strong activity across credit and equity markets. Our clients have remained resilient, And as AI and massive capital investment reshape markets, what we are seeing is that trusted benchmarks and data matter more than ever. In the debt markets, there was strong demand for rated debt in the quarter.

The issuance environment was favorable, with the impact of higher treasury yields offset by continued near record tight credit spreads. And S and P Global remains the rating agency of choice for AI related and hyperscaler issuance. We continue to see above average returns in the US equities market, and we made good progress in high growth adjacencies like DeFi and prediction markets. In energy, customers are adapting to geopolitical and supply chain volatility. Our global trading services business stabilized in the third quarter. And renewals are returning to the levels we saw prior to the Iran conflict. Demand for our AI products is also very strong.

During the quarter, we combined our MCP tools and adaptive retrieval agents, into 1 holistic AI data portal offering. Demand for our mission critical data is very strong, and we launched ratings, energy, and visible alpha data in MCP. During the quarter. What we hear consistently from customers is that they are choosing S&P Global Data because it is highly performant with lower error rates compared to other providers. And our adaptive retrieval agents are also resonating strongly with customers. We signed a large multiyear competitive displacement in the quarter, that combined Cap IQ with our AI data portal solutions from Market Intelligence.

We also signed a very large deal with a global energy company that combined an upstream win back with our AI-ready data. Negotiations with customers on AI rights are normalizing, and we are signing deals with robust pricing, that protect our IP. Customers see the value in leveraging our AI-ready data while respecting our intellectual property. Sales cycles stabilized, following some temporary noise last quarter, contributing to the acceleration in subscription revenue growth in both market intelligence and energy. The strength of the S and P Global Ratings franchise was clear in the third quarter. With total build issuance up 8% year over year.

The first 3 quarters of this year are the 3 strongest quarters on record for build issuance. Hyperscaler issuance remained strong in the quarter, bringing the year to date total to approximately $240 billion, and we continue to expect between $250 billion and $300 billion for the full year. We have seen continued strength in investment grade issuance outside of the hyperscalers. Excluding hyperscaler issuance in the third quarter, investment grade issuance would have increased around 15%. While total build issuance would have been up low single digits. We expect issuance to remain robust in absolute terms, but we are lapping a difficult year over year compare in the second half.

Our updated guidance assumes high single digit build issuance growth for the full year reflecting our continued expectations for $250 billion to $300 billion hyperscaler issuance. We now expect 20% to 30% growth in M&A issuance this year given the strength of M&A related issuance in the third quarter. Moving on to indices. S&P Dow Jones Indices remains the global leader in indices, both in terms of assets under management and in index based derivatives. We had more than $600 billion in net inflows into our ETF products, and we ended the quarter with ETF assets under management up 26%. Continued market volatility drove a 15% in average daily volumes for our exchange traded derivatives.

The strength of this franchise creates powerful opportunities for partnerships and collaboration in new and existing markets. We announced several agreements in the last few months that demonstrate the importance of partnering with S&P Dow Jones Indices, for leading market participants. The extension of our 500 options agreement with CBOE solidifies our partnership through the next 25 years and creates meaningful value for customers and shareholders. We are actively pursuing opportunities to expand the addressable market for our intellectual property in areas like prediction markets. And we continue to innovate and explore opportunities in partnerships that take advantage of the rapid innovation in this space. Enabling our customers to leverage our products in new ways.

We do not expect these announcements to have a meaningful impact on 2026 financial results. But we do expect to benefit in 2027 and beyond. As we expected, energy revenue growth accelerated in the quarter, though energy and commodities markets remain volatile. Oil prices remain elevated, and we expect oil to stay around $100 per barrel through the fourth quarter. We saw better traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with flows reaching almost 2-thirds pre-war levels. That made it easier for customers to transact with confidence and drive subscription growth in the quarter. We are also seeing market participants return to the derivative products based on our benchmark prices, as traders and others adjust to more volatile markets.

LNG refined products and chemicals remain more constrained. And our customers are using our data to help identify and plan for alternative sources and partnerships. I would also say our recent acquisition of Data Center Hawk could not have been timelier. Combined with 1 Research, S and P Global is now a leading provider of data and insights. Demand for data center build out is unprecedented. With our teams forecasting significant increases in demand for power, chips, and materials to deliver that infrastructure. In fact, our team forecasts nearly $900 billion of CapEx this year for the 6 largest hyperscalers, nearly doubling from 2025 levels.

The intensity of investment in this area is benefiting every 1 of our divisions, highlighting the growing convergence between financial markets and commodity markets. Obviously, this year, debt issuance and equity valuations have been driven higher by AI and data center investments. Demand is also increasing for supply chain insights, counterparty credit analytics, power forecasts, and logistics data, among financial services and industrial customers who need to understand these dynamics in-depth. Demand for our AI products is strong. For several quarters, customers using our AI solutions have increased their spend with us at a much faster rate than average. In market intelligence, ACV growth is now 1.8x the growth rate of non AI customers. In energy, it remains approximately 3x.

This is a strong signal of the value of our AI solutions to our customers. Over time, we believe growth rates will converge as more of our customers become AI customers. API call volume grew rapidly, up nearly 50% since Q2 and more than 4 thousand% year over year. More customers are expanding in house solutions and integrations with Frontier models powered by our data. Negotiations with customers on AI rights are normalizing, and we are signing deals with robust pricing that protect our IP. As I mentioned earlier, that comes down to the quality of our AI tools, and our unique datasets like Visible Alpha. Turning to slide 11.

We announced today that we have initiated a strategic review of alternatives for Capital IQ and its associated data businesses within Market Intelligence, including their potential separation. The businesses being considered for separation include the Capital IQ and the Kensho data and platforms businesses within Market Intelligence. While the exact perimeter remains under review, we expect to retain ratings direct, and ratings express as well as Enterprise Solutions. These businesses operate at scale with high recurring revenue and a large, long-standing base of more than 15 thousand clients and more than 355 thousand users. Demand for their trusted data continues to grow, as customers increasingly seek to integrate it directly into their own systems and tools.

We are confident in the ability of these businesses to create incredible value for our customers while rapidly innovating to bring differentiated data and insights to the market in an AI first way. We believe separate ownership would give them the dedicated investment and focus needed to continue the revenue growth acceleration and rapid innovation that we delivered this quarter. Given the commercial and data relationships between S&P Global and the business under review, we would seek to keep our interest closely aligned in any transaction.

At the same time, a more focused S and P Global would allow us to prioritize investment and reinforce our strengths in the markets where we have the strongest position, and are best enabled to create value. S and P Global is deeply embedded in the world's credit equities and commodities markets. Providing trusted benchmarks, mission critical data, and insights that are essential to how those markets operate. Our expected go forward portfolio benefits from durable secular tailwinds and attractive incremental margins. This allows us to invest while delivering consistent margin expansion over time.

We expect that when and if this process is completed, S and P Global will be a focused and synergistic organization of high growth businesses positioned for strong growth in organic revenue, profits, and EPS. We believe this portfolio can also generate significant free cash flow enhancing our capital allocation flexibility, and ultimately, our ability to return capital to shareholders. There is no definitive timetable for completing this strategic review. What I can tell you is that maintaining continuity for our customers and our colleagues throughout this process is of the utmost importance.

Existing contracts and service commitments remain in place, and we will ensure that our valued customers continue to receive the innovative products, differentiated data that they rely on today. While this process is underway, we will be thoughtful about the impact it could have on our customers, our people and our shareholders. We will provide updates at appropriate times, but we are very early in this process. And we expect the earliest meaningful update we would be able to provide will be on our February earnings call. With subscription growth accelerating, margins expanding, and an improving outlook, we are pleased with the excellent results we delivered in the third quarter.

We are excited about the opportunities to come for Capital IQ and its related businesses, and we are excited about the prospects for S and P Global. We look forward to finishing the year strong. Now I will hand it over to Eric to take you through the details of the quarter and the guidance.

Eric Walter Aboaf:Thank you, Martina, and good morning, everyone. Starting with Slide 14, We delivered a strong third quarter financial result with 7% revenue growth both on an organic constant currency and all in basis as M&A and FX had only modest net impacts. We saw revenue acceleration in 3 of our 4 divisions, which I will come back to shortly. Adjusted expenses grew 5% as we invested in key growth areas, funded with productivity initiatives and held total headcount flat year over year. We thus delivered 60 basis points of year on year margin expansion to 53.5%. Excluding Astra from the prior year period, our third quarter 2026 margin expansion would have been up 120 basis points.

We delivered 8% growth in adjusted operating profit and 9% growth in EPS, driven by more than $6 billion in share repurchases over the last 12 months, including another $2.6 billion in share buybacks launched in the third quarter, EPS growth was partly tempered by the timing of tax expenses. in the quarter. I will now turn to our divisions, starting with ratings on Slide 15. Ratings revenue grew 2% in the quarter. As expected, growth moderated from the first half of the year against tougher comparisons. Issuance was up 8% and transaction revenue increased 1%.

Both were led by considerable strength in investment grade up 28%, benefited from several large M&A and hyperscaler deals, partly offset by high yield bank loans and structured finance, all of which had difficult prior year comparisons. This quarter, the mix shift out of high yield and bank loans into investment grade led to a wider than usual variance between billed issuance growth and transaction revenue growth. However, year to date, that variance shrinks to less than 2 percentage points, with issuance and revenue growth up 15%, 13%, respectively. We expect build issuance growth to generally mirror transaction revenue growth over time. Nontransaction revenue grew 4% primarily driven by higher annual fee revenue as well as CRISIL.

Growth in nontransaction decelerated modestly given the much tougher comparison which will continue into the fourth quarter as well. When looking at combined transaction and non transaction revenue, as you can see on the slide, the 10% growth in financials and 8% growth in CRISIL and other revenue was tempered somewhat by the slower growth in governments and corporates, as well as a modest decline in structured finance. All that said, we are also very pleased to have closed the OwenZeppelin acquisition yesterday, gives us a leading position in the smart contract space and reinforces our progress in DeFi.

Adjusted expenses increased by 7% driven by higher compensation costs and continued investments in strategic initiatives partially offset by our productivity efforts. While margins contracted approximately 130 basis points in the quarter, this can be impacted by the timing of expenses. Year to date, ratings margins have expanded just over 100 basis points. Now turning to S and P Dow Jones Indices on Slide 16. Indices maintained its strong momentum, reporting the 14th consecutive quarter of record revenue. Revenue in the quarter grew 20% with strength in both asset linked fees and exchange traded derivatives.

Revenues associated with asset linked fees grew 24% year over year with growth driven by a balanced mix of market appreciation, and net inflows into products based on S and P Dow Jones indices. As the world's largest index business by AUM, we achieved a new record quarter for ETF AUM of $6.5 trillion in the quarter, and our strategic initiatives are contributing to a number 1 ranking in total ETF market flow capture among index providers. Exchange traded derivatives revenue increased 19% its fourth consecutive quarter of double digit growth, led by strength in SPX ETD volumes. Last month, as Martina mentioned, together with CBOE Global Markets, we announced the extension of our exclusive licensing agreement through 2051.

The new agreement builds on more than 40 years of collaboration and positions us well to drive further innovation and growth. The contract extension will not impact 2026 financial results, but we do expect a couple percentage points of incremental total index revenue growth in 2027. We will provide more detail when we give 2027 guidance in February. Data and custom subscriptions revenue grew 7% or 5% organically. Supported by continued new business growth in end of day contracts. Adjusted expenses were up 14% year over year driven by investments in growth initiatives, and higher compensation costs. Indices operating profit grew 22% and operating margin expanded a 150 basis points to 71.9%.

Now turning to S and P Global Energy on Slide 17. Energy revenue rebounded to 6% on both a reported and organic constant currency basis, benefiting from continued strong demand for Platts benchmarks. As well as our differentiated data research and thought leadership. We delivered this healthy growth despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and the negative impact of sanctions worth about half a point. In the third quarter, we saw improvements in the operating environment. Impacted customers in the Middle East have begun to stabilize and adapt to the current landscape. This was reflected in our accelerating organic growth rising sales, and solid GTS volumes.

The near term environment remains uncertain, but we continue to believe these headwinds are transitory and we continue to expect organic constant currency growth to normalize in 2027 to within the 6% to 8% average range we outlined at our 2025 Investor Day. Sera grew 5% or 6% organically when accounting for the divestiture of Upstream Software. Organic growth benefited from the broad based increases across our offerings particularly insights and analytics and consulting. We remain pleased to see ongoing traction in our upstream data transformation with a return to positive revenue growth and encouraging feedback from our early customers of Titan. Platts revenue increased 7% in the quarter, driven by strong growth in price assessments.

Growth in GTS revenues stabilized from last quarter as well despite a challenging compare from last year. The third quarter of 2025 and the third quarter of 2026 were tied for the second highest quarterly revenue on record As Martina mentioned, demand for our AI products has been very strong, and our discrete AI products and energy contributed around 50 basis points to our revenue growth this quarter. Adjusted expenses grew by just 2% driving margin expansion of 190 basis points to 48.1%. Energy's modest expense growth in the quarter was driven by higher technology and compensation costs, almost fully offset by productivity programs and expense discipline. Turning to Market Intelligence on Slide 18.

Revenue growth accelerated to 7% on both the reported and organic constant currency basis in the third quarter, We saw particular strength in Kensho Data and Platforms, and Kensho Data itself was Market Intelligence's fastest growing business. We remain encouraged by the strong customer adoption and demand for our AI-ready data. Similar to our energy division, our discrete AI products contributed approximately 0.5 a point of growth to Kensho Data and Platforms this quarter. Sales cycles have normalized following a slight elongation last quarter. And we are no longer seeing a negative impact to revenue growth. In fact, we saw a small benefit in the quarter from some true ups on contracts that renewed after the second quarter ended.

We saw improved sales and renewal rates in 3Q, as we closed on several of the large deals that have extended from second quarter while also ensuring that our intellectual property was protected for the long term. In the third quarter, subscription revenue grew 6%, and 7% on an organic basis, benefiting from broad based growth across our subscription franchises. Kensho Data and Platforms revenue growth accelerated to 10% or 6% organically. Saw acceleration in Kensho data driven by strong adoption of our AI-ready data feeds with growth comfortably in the double digits. Enterprise solutions reported revenue grew 2% reflecting the divestiture of EDM and ThinkFolio while organic revenue was up a strong 8%.

This was driven by broad based growth across products particularly in lending solutions like WSO. Enterprise Solutions organic subscription revenue grew 7% also driven by strength across products. This performance really demonstrated the critical nature of these products in our customers' workflows and also in the markets themselves. Market Intelligence's adjusted expenses increased 5% year over year, driven by inorganic expenses from the Wit Intelligence acquisition as well as higher technology costs, partially offset by the impact of recent divestitures and productivity programs. Market Intelligence delivered 110 basis points of operating margin expansion to 36.2% in the quarter. Now shifting to our outlook starting with Slide 19.

As a reminder, with our spin of Mobility completed on July 1, mobility results were moved to discontinued operations. Consistent with the guidance we provided in the second quarter, our full year guide on both the GAAP and adjusted basis excludes the contributions from Mobility for the whole year. Slide 19 outlines our GAAP guidance. Slide 20 shows our adjusted guidance. Given the outperformance in both ratings and indices year to date, we are raising our full year guidance for organic constant currency growth to a range of 7.5% to 8.5%. We are also increasing our guidance for adjusted operating margin expansion. We now expect total operating margin expansion in the range of 75 to 100 basis points.

Excluding the impact of Astra, which was divested late last year, we would expect margin expansion of 125 to 150 basis points. While we expect slightly higher interest expense as a result of the expected bond offering later this quarter, we expect the EPS impact to be more than offset by lower corporate unallocated expense and a lower share count. So we are raising our guidance for adjusted EPS as well to a range of $17.70 to $17.95. Now turning to our division guidance on Slide 21. As I mentioned, we are raising our outlook for ratings. Given our expectation for high single digit build issuance for the year.

We now expect organic constant currency revenue growth of 6.5% to 8%. In the fourth quarter, this implies a slight decline year over year in transaction revenue, as we have been signaling all year and a modest growth in non transaction revenue as we lap a difficult comparison from the fourth quarter of last year. For the full year, we expect ratings margin expansion to be towards the lower end of the 75 to 100 basis point range we just discussed for the company as a whole. For indices, we now expect organic constant currency growth in the range of 17% to 18.5%, as we continue to benefit from strong equity valuations and strong net flows.

For the full year, we expect indices margins to be towards the higher end of the 75 to 100 basis point company range.
